title: Data provenance, survivorship and revisions

objectives.text: Reconstruct a bounded synthetic point-in-time snapshot by observation/availability/revision, retaining source lineage and rejecting ambiguous revision keys.
Explain survivorship/universe and omitted-delisting bias with a worked historical-universe return, and distinguish complete terminal returns from missing data.

blocks.markdown: A result needs a trail from original source through download/vintage, immutable raw content hash, schema, parser/version, units/timezone/identifier mapping, filters, corporate-action rules and transformations to input/output. Hashes detect byte differences, not authenticity, correctness or availability. Record permissions/licensing and what may be redistributed. This lesson uses own synthetic integer timestamps and cents, not a live vendor dataset. A permanent identifier avoids treating a reused ticker as the same security, but identifier mappings themselves need dated lineage.

Observation/event time says what period or event a value describes. Available time says when this research process could first use that revision, after publication plus declared ingestion/processing delay. Retrieval time today is another timestamp, not proof that today's values existed historically. ALFRED stores vintages/real-time periods for originally released and revised economic observations. Its date-level vintage is not by itself an intraday timestamp or proof a particular trader had the value at the open.

blocks.title: An old observation can acquire a new value later

steps.text: A observation 1 first becomes available at 2, value 100. A correction becomes available at 5, value 120. At decision 3, use 100, not 120, even though both rows describe observation 1.

At cutoff 3, B observation 1 value 200 is also available. A observation 3 value 110 is available only at 4 and excluded. At cutoff 5 both A observations remain in this full snapshot, with observation 1 revised to 120.

The selector chooses the latest available revision FOR EACH (asset,observation), not merely the single most recent observation per asset. Downstream lag/window features must still choose the intended observation window and missing/stale policy.

blocks.caption: Expected snapshots: cutoff 3((A,1,2,0,100),(B,1,2,0,200)); cutoff 5((A,1,5,1,120),(A,3,4,0,110),(B,1,2,0,200)); duplicate revision key; historical equal-weight return -9/20; survivor-only 1/10. Exact Python output uses quoted strings. Input is fully validated first, max 128 rows, integer timestamps, positive cents, unique revision keys and nondecreasing availability by revision. Same-time revisions use greater revision ID. No missing-value or retraction semantics implemented; do not drop such source events silently.

blocks.markdown: A correct price join does not fix the wrong universe. Choosing today's index constituents, currently listed funds or surviving stocks and testing them backward conditions on future survival/membership. Reconstruct eligibility and membership using dated, available-at-the-time information, including entries/exits, name/identifier changes and delistings. Survivorship bias often inflates results, but the direction/magnitude depends on strategy and selection;do not claim every filter has a fixed positive bias.

Own arithmetic: two historically eligible assets begin equally weighted, A total return +10%, B terminal total return -100% after a known-worthless liquidation. Portfolio return=(0.10-1.00)/2=-0.45. Dropping B because it is absent today gives +0.10 instead. The -100% is stated terminal evidence in this synthetic case, NOT a rule that every delisting is worthless. Delisting can mean mergers, exchange transfers or other events. Missing terminal return is unknown, not zero and not automatically -100%; retain reason and sensitivity policy.

CRSP describes active/inactive securities, permanent identifiers and corporate-action history. That coverage helps but does not independently prove any specific extract/query is bias free. Shumway's 1997 paper documents omitted delisting returns in a HISTORICAL CRSP sample; it is evidence of a failure mode, not a claim that today's CRSP files still have the same gaps or that a historical replacement estimate fits all markets. Inspect the actual extract/version/field semantics and terminal-cashflow policy.

Keep raw versions and a snapshot manifest linking source/version, available-at assumptions, code/configuration hashes, selected IDs/row counts, rejection reasons and transformed output. A later correction should produce a new research revision, not silently overwrite the old experiment. The pure selector returns an in-memory snapshot only; it does not authenticate timestamps, fetch historical universe membership, perform a licensed download or persist immutable archives.

Independent transfer: permute rows and verify the same sorted snapshot; add a future correction and confirm every earlier cutoff stays unchanged. Test exact availability boundary, zero rows, duplicate/conflicting revisions and a revision whose availability moves backward. Build dated universe membership separately and reproduce the two-asset return with explicit terminal evidence; then mark B terminal return missing and explain why neither zero nor -100% can be inserted without a policy/evidence change.

Sources: [ALFRED download/vintage semantics](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help/downloaddata), [ALFRED archive API overview](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/alfred.html), [CRSP active/inactive and permanent IDs](https://www.crsp.org/research/crsp-us-stock-databases-2025-layout/), [Shumway 1997 original historical delisting-bias paper](https://www.tylergshumway.org/Shumway-DelistingBiasCRSP-1997.pdf). Own rows/returns/interface are synthetic teaching design, not sourced market returns.

summary: Preserve lineage and distinguish observation, availability, retrieval and revision clocks. Correct historical values do not fix future-selected membership. Terminal returns need evidence; missing does not mean zero or automatic total loss. This pure bounded selector is not a vendor archive/universe service.
